# sq-36 — Exact null spellings

`nullTokens` keys are the vocabulary entries (`null`, `NA`, empty, ...), matched case-insensitively after trimming, so `NULL`, `Null`, `null` and ` NULL ` all count under one key, and the counts include all-null (separator) rows. A consumer that treats only one spelling as null cannot get its count. Add the exact spellings as seen, and counts that leave out all-null rows. **Not in this slice:** changing the vocabulary or how values are classified.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:** core

**2026-10-27** — Owner decision (2026-10-27), verbatim, on whether whitespace-only differences are distinct spellings: "trim whitespace, case insensitive for nulls. a null is a null." So exact spellings are not reported: NULL, Null, null and " NULL " stay one null. The exact-spellings part of this slice is dropped; what remains is re-scoped before it runs (the separator-row exclusion).

## Why

A library consumer treats only the exact token `NULL` as null and keeps other spellings as text. It can only report squalify's counts as upper bounds today, and has to subtract the separator rows itself.

- In a file with all-null separator rows, each field's null counts are also reported without those rows, and the two add up.
- Values that differ only in surrounding whitespace are reported as distinct spellings (or the trim rule is stated; pick one and document it).
